title: QT Imaging Delivers Strong Second Quarter Growth While Building the Foundation for Commercial Scale
summary: Second-quarter revenue reached $7.4 million; first-half revenue increased 116% to $14.0 million, with 28 scanners shipped Strengthened capital…...
body_text: QT Imaging Delivers Strong Second Quarter Growth While Building the Foundation for Commercial Scale August 12, 2026 4:05pm EDT Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio 10-Q HTML XBRL Zip Second-quarter revenue reached $7.4 million; first-half revenue increased 116% to $14.0 million, with 28 scanners shipped Strengthened capital position through a $10.0 million public offering and expanded direct U.S. commercial capabilities to accelerate adoption Reaffirms full-year 2026 revenue guidance of approximately $39 million Conference Call begins at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time today NOVATO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- QT Imaging Holding, Inc. (Nasdaq: QTI) (“QT Imaging” or the “Company”), a medical device company dedicated to transforming breast health management through innovative, radiation-free imaging technology, today reported financial results for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, and provided a business update. “Our second quarter results demonstrate continued execution and the growing commercial momentum of QT Imaging. Revenue more than doubled year-over-year to $7.4 million, and we shipped fifteen Breast Acoustic CT scanners during the quarter, compared with eight in the prior-year period,” said Dr. Raluca Dinu, Chief Executive Officer of QT Imaging. “We also took important steps to support continued growth, completing a $10 million public offering, expanding our direct U.S. sales organization, and securing regulatory authorization in Israel and Saudi Arabia. At the same time, we generated new evidence demonstrating less than 1% variability in Speed of Sound measurements across our scanners, successfully completed our first routine FDA inspection with zero Form 483 observations, and expanded manufacturing capacity through our new 22,000-square-foot facility. These are tangible steps toward scaling Breast Acoustic CT commercially while building the clinical, regulatory and operational foundation for broader adoption.” “With more than 12,000 women already imaged using our technology, we are building more than an innovative medical imaging system; we are building a quantitative breast imaging platform that integrates advanced hardware, software, cloud infrastructure and, over time, AI-enabled clinical applications,” added Dr. Dinu. “At the same time, we continue to evolve our commercial strategy by complementing our established distribution partnerships with expanded direct commercial, and business development capabilities to accelerate customer engagement and broaden adoption. While geopolitical developments have impacted commercial activities in parts of the Gulf region, we are beginning to see encouraging signs of renewed customer engagement.” Second Quarter and Recent Business Highlights Continued commercial execution: QT Imaging shipped 15 Breast Acoustic CT scanners during the second quarter of 2026 and 28 scanners during the first six months of the year. The revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $7.4 million. The Company continues to pursue commercial opportunities through a combination of established distribution partners and its expanding internal commercial and business development capabilities. Strengthened capital position: During the second quarter, QT Imaging completed an underwritten public offering that generated approximately $10.0 million in gross proceeds. The Company also extended the maturity of its senior secured term loan by two years, from March 31, 2027, to March 31, 2029. Built a scalable U.S. commercial organization: Under the leadership of our Chief Commercial Officer Satrajit Misra, a seasoned medical imaging executive with three decades of industry experience, QT Imaging expanded its direct commercial organization with the appointments of Jason Dyer as Vice President, Regional Sales East, and Dave Reinhart as Vice President, Regional Sales West. Together, this team strengthens the Company’s ability to directly engage breast imaging centers, clinicians and enterprise health systems, deepen strategic customer relationships and complement its established distribution partnerships, creating a scalable commercial model designed to accelerate adoption, grow the installed base and support long-term revenue growth and margin expansion. Expanded global regulatory foundation for Breast Acoustic CT scanners: During the quarter, the Company received AMAR authorization from Israel’s Ministry of Health and Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) regulatory clearance in Saudi Arabia. QT Imaging continues to pursue additional regulatory authorizations in the Gulf region and Europe. Successfully completed the Company’s first routine FDA inspection: The inspection concluded with zero Form 483 observations, reflecting the strength of the Company’s Quality Management System and its focus on quality, compliance and manufacturing readiness. Generated additional scientific evidence: A multi-site repeatability and reproducibility study demonstrated less than 1% variability in Speed of Sound measurements across Breast Acoustic CT scanners. The results support the potential use of objective and reproducible quantitative imaging biomarkers in longitudinal breast health assessment and treatment monitoring. These results reflect testing performed under the study conditions and do not represent a new FDA-cleared indication. Continued advancing the QTI technology platform: Development activities included enhancements to image reconstruction, quantitative imaging algorithms, clinical workflow, and the QTI Precision Pathway™ cloud platform. The Company also continued its collaboration with Olea Medical to productize its multimodality image viewer, physician workflow and quantitative image analysis. Strengthened clinical and scientific leadership: Appointed Dr. Julia Albright as Chief Science Officer, effective July 27, 2026, and welcomed nationally recognized breast surgical oncologist Dr. Barry Roseman as Senior Medical Advisor. Dr. Albright brings more than three decades of leadership in medical imaging innovation, quantitative imaging and artificial intelligence, with a proven track record of translating advanced technologies into clinically impactful products. Dr. Roseman brings more than 30 years of experience in breast cancer diagnosis, treatment and multidisciplinary patient care, providing deep clinical expertise to support physician engagement, clinical implementation, and broader adoption of our technology. Advanced clinical expansion in Israel: Following our recent AMAR authorization from Israel’s Ministry of Health, the first Breast Acoustic CT scanner in Israel is planned for placement at Rambam Health Care Campus, one of the country’s leading academic medical centers. The scanner will support a planned clinical study evaluating Breast Acoustic CT imaging modality in women with hereditary risk for breast cancer, expanding the Company’s clinical evidence-generation efforts in an important high-risk population. Expanded manufacturing capacity while improving operating efficiency: Continued investing in manufacturing excellence and supply chain readiness while relocating to a new 22,000-square-foot headquarters and manufacturing facility, located in Petaluma, CA. The expanded facility provides more than 2.5x the operational space of the current location while reducing lease cost per square foot by approximately 55%, enhancing the Company's ability to scale production efficiently. Increased visibility within the investment community: QT Imaging was added to the Russell Microcap® Index as part of the 2026 semi-annual Russell index reconstitution and following its return to the Nasdaq Capital Market in January. Pursued grassroots initiatives focused on breast health: Dr. Dinu participated in two prestigious events hosted by The Shift, including its inaugural Shiftmakers Gala celebrating women driving change held at Harvard University and featuring actress and breast cancer survivor Olivia Munn, and presenting the Shiftmaker Award to tennis legend and two-time cancer survivor Martina Navratilova at the Sports Shiftmaker Awards ceremony during Wimbledon week in London. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $7.4 million, an increase of 103% compared with $3.7 million for the second quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the shipment of fifteen Breast Acoustic CT scanners in the 2026 quarter, compared with eight in the prior-year quarter. Gross margin was 41% for the second quarter of 2026, compared with 50% for the second quarter of 2025. The gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 was in line with our projections for sales in the USA. The higher prior-year gross margin reflected a lower weighted average cost of inventory sold. Total operating expenses were $4.9 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared with $2.9 million for the second quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to employee compensation and benefits, professional service costs, and marketing expenses. Operating loss for the second quarter of 2026 was $1.9 million, compared with an operating loss of $1.0 million, for the second quarter of 2025 and $2.3 million for the first quarter of 2026. Total interest and other expense, net, was $9.2 million during the second quarter of 2026, compared with $3.0 million in the prior-year quarter. The increase was due primarily to an $8.3 million non-cash loss on debt extinguishment related to the Lynrock Lake term loan modification. Net loss for the second quarter of 2026 was $11.1 million, or $0.75 per share, compared with a net loss of $4.0 million, or $0.42 per share, for the second quarter of 2025. Prior-period share and per-share amounts have been adjusted to reflect the Company’s 3:1 reverse stock split completed in October 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, which excludes interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, other income or expense, changes in the fair value of financial liabilities, and stock-based compensation, was negative $1.2 million, or $0.08 per share, for the second quarter of 2026, compared with negative $0.8 million, or $0.08 per share, for the second quarter of 2025. Net cash used in operating activities during the second quarter of 2026 was $4.8 million, compared with $1.4 million during the second quarter of 2025. As of June 30, 2026, the Company had cash and restricted cash of $11.0 million, compared with $10.5 million as of December 31, 2025. As of August 7, 2026, the Company had cash and restricted cash of $14.2 million. 2026 Revenue Outlook The Company affirms its 2026 revenue guidance of approximately $39 million. This outlook reflects minimum order quantities under its distribution agreements, as well as expected contributions from the Company’s direct sales efforts. Conference Call and Webcast QT Imaging management will host a conference call today at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time to discuss these results and provide a business update. Participants are encouraged to pre-register here . Callers who are unable to pre-register can access the call by dialing 866-777-2509 (U.S.) or 412-317-5413 (international). A live and archived webcast of the call will be available at this link and on the IR Calendar section of the QT Imaging website. Non-GAAP Financial Measures Some of the financial information and data contained in this press release, such as EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA, have not been prepared in accordance with GAAP. To supplement our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP in our press release, we also report certain non-GAAP financial measures. A “non-GAAP financial measure” refers to a numerical measure of a company’s historical or future financial performance, financial position or cash flows that excludes (or includes) amounts that are included in (or excluded from) the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP in such company’s financial statements. Non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the relevant GAAP measures and should be read in conjunction with information presented on a GAAP basis. Because not all companies use identical calculations, our presentation of non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies. The presentation of these financial measures is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, financial information prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP and should not be considered measures of QT Imaging’s liquidity. Investors are cautioned that there are material limitations associated with the use of non-GAAP financial measures as an analytical tool. In particular, many of the adjustments to our GAAP financial measures reflect the exclusion of certain items, as defined in our non-GAAP definitions below, which are recurring and will be reflected in our financial results for the foreseeable future. title: Wieczór z kasynem online: wygoda, atmosfera i pomoc na wyciągnięcie ręki

body_text: Kasyno online coraz częściej staje się formą wieczornej rozrywki dla dorosłych, którzy cenią swobodę, przejrzystość i możliwość korzystania z atrakcji bez wychodzenia z domu. Nie chodzi wyłącznie o same gry. Całe doświadczenie zaczyna się już w chwili otwarcia strony: od spokojnej nawigacji, przez czytelne informacje, aż po poczucie, że w razie pytań można szybko znaleźć odpowiedź. Pierwsze wrażenie ma znaczenie Po wejściu na dobrze przygotowaną platformę użytkownik nie powinien czuć się zagubiony. Menu zazwyczaj prowadzi do najważniejszych obszarów, a opisy poszczególnych sekcji pomagają zorientować się, co właściwie znajduje się w ofercie. Przejrzysty układ pozwala skupić się na atmosferze wieczoru, zamiast tracić czas na poszukiwanie podstawowych informacji. Wygoda ma także wymiar praktyczny. Strona dopasowana do telefonu umożliwia korzystanie z rozrywki podczas odpoczynku na kanapie, a wersja komputerowa zapewnia większy obraz i bardziej przestronny układ. Dla wielu dorosłych użytkowników ważne jest również to, aby przejście między poszczególnymi częściami serwisu było płynne i nie wymagało przyzwyczajania się do skomplikowanych rozwiązań. Osoby zainteresowane szczegółami dotyczącymi niewielkich wpłat mogą sięgnąć po kasyno online blik depozyt 10 zł , gdzie zebrano informacje związane z takim sposobem zasilenia konta. Tego rodzaju materiały są przydatne wtedy, gdy ktoś chce najpierw spokojnie zapoznać się z dostępnymi możliwościami i zrozumieć, jak wygląda obsługa płatności. Rozrywka dopasowana do nastroju Jednego wieczoru liczy się dynamika i kolorowa oprawa, innym razem większe znaczenie ma spokojne tempo oraz elegancki wygląd stołu. Kasyna internetowe próbują odpowiadać na różne nastroje, oferując szeroki wybór formatów rozrywki. Dzięki temu użytkownik może po prostu przeglądać dostępne propozycje i wybrać tę, która najlepiej pasuje do chwili. Dużą rolę odgrywa oprawa wizualna. Animacje, dźwięki i układ ekranu budują atmosferę podobną do tej znanej z tradycyjnych salonów, choć w bardziej kameralnym wydaniu. Dla części odbiorców atrakcyjna jest możliwość obserwowania rozgrywki prowadzonej przez prezentera, a dla innych liczy się przede wszystkim dyskretna, domowa forma kontaktu z cyfrową rozrywką. czytelne opisy dostępnych stołów i automatów, sprawne działanie na telefonie oraz komputerze, wyraźne informacje o płatnościach i historii operacji, łatwy dostęp do ustawień konta oraz centrum pomocy. Wsparcie, które nie komplikuje sprawy Najlepsze doświadczenie pojawia się wtedy, gdy pomoc jest obecna, ale nie przytłacza. W dobrze zaprojektowanym serwisie centrum pomocy odpowiada na najczęstsze pytania prostym językiem. Użytkownik może sprawdzić znaczenie poszczególnych komunikatów, dowiedzieć się, gdzie znaleźć historię aktywności albo ustalić, jak skontaktować się z obsługą. Ważna jest także forma kontaktu. Krótka wiadomość do konsultanta, formularz albo rozmowa na czacie pozwalają wyjaśnić sprawę bez konieczności przeszukiwania wielu podstron. Dla dorosłego odbiorcy, który korzysta z kasyna po pracy lub późnym wieczorem, liczy się przede wszystkim konkretna odpowiedź i spokojny ton, bez zbędnych formalności. Przejrzystość dotyczy również komunikatów dotyczących środków, czasu realizacji operacji oraz ustawień konta. Jeśli informacje są podane w jasny sposób, łatwiej zachować kontrolę nad całym doświadczeniem i uniknąć nieporozumień. Pomoc nie powinna być ukrytym dodatkiem, lecz naturalną częścią platformy, podobnie jak ustawienia języka czy powiadomienia. Wieczór po swojemu Jedną z największych zalet rozrywki online jest możliwość dopasowania jej do własnego rytmu. Nie trzeba planować wyjścia, rezerwować czasu ani dostosowywać się do atmosfery panującej w lokalu. Można rozpocząć spokojny wieczór po kolacji, zrobić przerwę, a następnie wrócić do przeglądania oferty wtedy, gdy pojawi się na to ochota. Ta swoboda dobrze współgra z potrzebą prywatności. Dorosły użytkownik sam decyduje, kiedy korzysta z serwisu i jak długo chce pozostać w cyfrowym świecie rozrywki. Przydatne są ustawienia przypomnień oraz narzędzia pozwalające określić własne ramy korzystania. Nie odbierają one przyjemności, lecz pomagają zachować porządek i sprawiają, że wieczór pozostaje świadomą formą odpoczynku. Warto docenić także możliwość szybkiego porównywania informacji. Czytelne opisy, widoczne zasady poszczególnych formatów oraz uporządkowane dane sprawiają, że użytkownik nie musi polegać na domysłach. Dzięki temu uwaga może skupić się na samej atmosferze i estetyce serwisu, a nie na rozszyfrowywaniu niejasnych komunikatów. Nowoczesna wygoda bez zbędnego zamieszania Kasyno online najlepiej sprawdza się jako dopracowana forma rozrywki dla dorosłych: dostępna, estetyczna i wspierana przez sprawną obsługę. Liczy się nie tylko bogata oferta, lecz także to, jak łatwo odnaleźć potrzebne informacje, jak szybko uzyskać pomoc i czy całość działa naturalnie na wybranym urządzeniu. Właśnie połączenie wygody, przejrzystości i przyjaznej atmosfery decyduje o jakości doświadczenia. Gdy platforma nie komplikuje prostych czynności, oferuje jasne komunikaty i pozwala korzystać z pomocy bez skrępowania, wieczorna rozrywka staje się bardziej komfortowa. To spokojny, współczesny sposób na spędzenie czasu, w którym użytkownik zachowuje własne tempo i może skupić się na przyjemności odkrywania cyfrowego świata kasyna.

title: 18 Questions To Ask In Your Next Software Demo | Roofr
summary: Going into a roofing software demo? Use this complete question checklist to evaluate vendors on key features, pricing, support, integrations, and red flags.
body_text: TL;DR Choose your roofing software confidently by getting answers to the questions that matter. See a breakdown of the right questions to ask at each stage of the demo. Before your next roofing software sales demo, come in prepped with a list of questions to ask. More often than not, people sit back in demos and let the salesperson do their thing. The vendor controls what you see, the order you see it in, and how much time gets spent on each feature. But it's really up to you to decide what’s important, and that requires some prep. If you're not asking the right questions, it's easy to walk out of a 45-minute call feeling excited about software that's completely wrong for your business. Not only is that a waste of your time, but it could also be a big waste of money. 74% of roofers spend at least $5,000 per year on technology . That's a real budget line, and the questions below will help you spend it on something that actually provides value. Asking pointed questions in demos will help you uncover: What kind of support they actually offer customers, How they treat you after you've signed up, Whether this software will work for you in the long run, Any hidden fees that'll come out of the woodwork later. Refer to the checklist below before, during, and after any roofing software demo. → Check out 6 Ways Roofing Software Can Help You Earn More Money to see the impact roofing software can have on your business. Core features: 1. Can you walk me through a complete end-to-end workflow — from entering a new lead to sending a final invoice? This is the single most revealing question you can ask. If the workflow feels clunky or broken at any point, that's exactly what you'll deal with every day. 2. How are roof measurements handled? Is satellite measurement built in, or do I need a separate tool? Switching between platforms to get measurements into your estimates adds time and introduces errors. Find out upfront whether this is seamless or duct-taped together. 3. Can proposals include photos, line items, and multiple pricing tiers (good/better/best)? These aren't nice-to-haves anymore. They're what separates a proposal that wins jobs from one that looks like a spreadsheet printout. 4. Does the CRM support pipeline views and automated follow-up sequences? Automated follow-up is one of the highest-leverage features in roofing software. If it's missing or clunky, you'll be stuck doing that manually forever. Setup and ease of use: 6. How long does onboarding typically take, and who handles the setup? Implementation surprises, both in time and cost, are one of the most common complaints from contractors who switch software. Get the onboarding details in writing so you know exactly what to expect. 7. What does training look like, and is it included in the price? Many software companies charge extra for implementation support. Roofr doesn't, but plenty of others do, and it's easy to miss that detail in a contract. 8. Do other roofing businesses like mine use this tool? Can you share any examples or case studies? Roofing is a unique industry with workflows that don't map to generic contractor software. If the vendor can't point to roofing-specific use cases, that's your answer. Pricing and contracts: 9. What's included in the base price, and what costs extra? The demo price is rarely the full price. Ask specifically about features that looked standard but might be add-ons. 10. How many users can I have, and how much does it cost to add more? Per-seat pricing is common and can significantly inflate your monthly cost as your team grows. Know the pricing ceiling before you sign. 11. What's the contract length, and what are the cancellation terms? If they dodge this question or make cancellation sound complicated, assume getting out is going to be painful. Integrations and data: 12. Does this integrate with QuickBooks (or my accounting software), and how does that sync work? Manual data entry between your roofing software and accounting system is a time sink and an error factory. Integration should be seamless, not approximate. 13. What happens to my data if I decide to leave? Is it exportable? Your customer history, job records, and financials belong to you. Make sure you can take them with you if you ever decide to leave. Customer support: 14. What does support look like day-to-day — phone, chat, email? And what are the hours? When something breaks mid-estimate on a storm day, "submit a ticket and we'll get back to you in 48 hours" is not an acceptable answer. Ask the sales rep, and then cross-reference company reviews to see what existing users say about customer support. 15. Do I get a dedicated point of contact, or is support handled by a general team? A dedicated contact who knows your account is genuinely different from being added to a queue every time there’s an issue. It's worth knowing which one you're getting. Product roadmap: 16. How often do you release updates? What has shipped in the last 12 months? Past update frequency is the most honest signal of whether a company is actively investing in the product or just maintaining it. Again, it’s good to cross-reference this with customer reviews to get the full story. 17. What's your process for customer feedback, and how does it influence what gets built? Asking if you can give feedback is different from understanding what actually happens to it. This question separates customer-driven companies from the ones that build whatever they want and expect you to go along with it. 18. What features are planned for the next 6–12 months? Any software company with a real roadmap should be able to answer this. If they can't, that's a sign. Red flags to watch out for in a roofing software demo Even when answers sound good, watch for these warning signs: They can't answer your questions live. If the rep needs to "check with the product team" on basic feature questions, that's a gap you'll feel as a customer. Their pricing packages don’t make sense. If they don’t allow you to customize a plan that fits your business needs, you may get stuck paying for features you won’t use. The demo only shows perfect pre-loaded data. Clean, curated demo environments don't show you how the tool handles messy real-world situations. They push for a same-day decision. Good software vendors want you to make the right choice. High-pressure closes on a first demo are a warning sign. Vague cancellation terms. If they dodge the question about cancelling, assume getting out is going to be painful. Ask more questions in roofing software demos Keep this list handy going into your next software demo, and don’t be afraid to lead the conversation. → Want the full list of software categories for roofers? Head over to 7 Essential Roofing Software Tools for our full breakdown. ‍ Roofing software demo FAQs How long should a roofing software demo take? A solid first demo is 30-45 minutes. That’s enough to cover core workflows and get your main questions answered. If you're seriously evaluating the platform, request a second, longer demo focused on your specific use cases. Should I invite my team to the demo? Yes, especially whoever will use the software day-to-day. The people running the tool will have different questions than the owner, and their buy-in is critical for actual adoption. How many demos should I do before deciding? Talk to at least 2-3 vendors for any significant software commitment. You'll ask better questions in the third demo than the first, and comparison makes evaluation much clearer. What's the most important thing to check in a roofing software demo? Watch the full workflow end-to-end, from lead to invoice. If it flows cleanly and matches how your business actually operates, that's the most reliable signal. Features are secondary to workflow fit. Can I trial the software before committing? It never hurts to ask. Most reputable vendors offer a trial period or pilot program. Be skeptical of platforms that won't let you test before signing a contract. ‍

title: KLX Energy Services Announces $125 Million Rights Offering for Common Stock Backstopped For Up to $94 Million to Reduce Leverage

body_text: Release Details KLX Energy Services Announces $125 Million Rights Offering for Common Stock Backstopped For Up to $94 Million to Reduce Leverage Aug 10, 2026 PDF Version 162.8 KB HOUSTON , Aug. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- KLX Energy Services Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: KLXE) ("KLX" or the "Company") announced today that the Company's Board of Directors has approved a $125 million backstopped rights offering (the "Rights Offering") available to all holders of record of the Company's common stock, par value $0.01 per share ("Common Stock"), as of 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on August 21, 2026 (the "Record Date"). The Rights Offering will be made through a distribution to all holders of record of Common Stock as of the Record Date of transferable subscription rights to purchase shares of Common Stock at a subscription price of $1.49 per share (the "Subscription Price"). Each holder of record of Common Stock as of the Record Date will receive one subscription right for each share of Common Stock owned (each, a "Right"). Each Right will entitle the holder to purchase 3.885 shares of Common Stock at the Subscription Price per share. The Company will not issue any fractional shares of Common Stock in the Rights Offering, and all exercises of subscription rights will be rounded down to the nearest whole share. In addition, the Company will not issue fractional subscription rights or pay cash in lieu of fractional subscription rights. The Rights Offering is currently expected to commence on August 24, 2026, and expire at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on September 23, 2026 (the "Expiration Date"). The rights being issued in the offering are expected to be listed for trading on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC under the symbol "KLXER" and therefore will be transferable. The Rights Offering is backstopped by the existing holders (the "Backstop Parties") of the Company's Senior Secured Floating Rate Cash / PIK Notes due 2030 (the "2030 Notes") in an aggregate backstop commitment amount of $94.0 million pursuant to a rights offering backstop agreement (the "Backstop Agreement"), with each individual Backstop Party subject to an aggregate 30% ownership limitation on a pro forma fully diluted basis. The backstop commitment may be increased up to $125.0 million if the Backstop Parties elect to increase their backstop commitment amounts prior to August 21, 2026. The Backstop Parties have committed to purchase, to the extent any shares of Common Stock remain unsubscribed following the exercise of any Rights and Over-Subscription Rights (as defined below) in the Rights Offering, their respective backstop commitment amounts through an exchange of their 2030 Notes (at 100% of the principal amount thereof plus accrued and unpaid interest) for shares of Common Stock at the Subscription Price (the "Backstop Exchange"). Upon completion of the Backstop Exchange, the outstanding principal amount of the 2030 Notes is expected to be reduced by $94.0 million as a result of the combination of par redemptions from any excess proceeds in the Rights Offering and the exchange of 2030 Notes for Common Stock in the Backstop Exchange. The Company intends to use any net cash proceeds it receives in connection with the Rights Offering up to $31.0 million for general corporate purposes, and for any amounts over $31.0 million, the Company intends to repurchase 2030 Notes at par, which is permitted under the Backstop Agreement. For shares purchased by Backstop Parties pursuant to the Backstop Exchange, the Company will cancel a principal amount of such Backstop Party's outstanding 2030 Notes equal to the applicable backstop commitment amount. Upon completion of the Backstop Exchange, the Company will enter into an amended and restated indenture governing the 2030 Notes (the "Amended and Restated Indenture"). The Amended and Restated Indenture provides the Company with additional operating and strategic flexibility and includes, among other things, the following benefits: (i) resets the total net leverage ratio maintenance covenant step-down schedule to provide additional runway to reduce leverage, (ii) relaxes the total net leverage ratio incurrence test for additional indebtedness from 2.50:1.00 to 3.00:1.00, (iii) permanently excludes capital lease obligations from the definition of "Indebtedness" for purposes of calculating financial maintenance covenant compliance, secured net leverage ratio, and any incurrence based test, ratio, or basket, (iv) increases the basket for indebtedness in respect of purchase money obligations and capital lease obligations from $75.0 million to $85.0 million, and (v) provides for par redemption of 2030 Notes in connection with the Backstop Exchange and excludes Rights Offering redemption proceeds from the excess cash flow sweep. In addition, the Amended and Restated Indenture resets the make-whole expiry date to two years from the effective date of the Amended and Restated Indenture and reduces the premium from 102% to 101%. The Rights Offering will include an over-subscription privilege to permit each rights holder that exercises its subscription rights in full to purchase additional shares of Common Stock (if any) that remain unsubscribed on the Expiration Date (the "Over-Subscription Right"). The availability of the over-subscription privilege will be subject to certain terms and restrictions to be set forth in the prospectus supplement, including that no holder will be entitled to exercise subscription rights (including any Over-Subscription Rights) in the Rights Offering to the extent such exercise would result in such holder, together with its affiliates and any persons acting in concert with such holder, beneficially owning more than 9.995% of the Company's outstanding Common Stock on a pro forma basis after giving effect to such exercise. The Rights Offering will be made pursuant to the Company's existing effective shelf registration statement on Form S-3 (Reg. No. 333-295905) on file with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") and a prospectus supplement (and the accompanying base prospectus) to be filed with the SEC prior to the commencement of the Rights Offering. title: How Do You Store Books?
summary: The best book storage ideas make your collection easy to access while using your available wall, floor, and furniture space efficiently. Depending on the size of your collection and your home, you can store books on floor-to-ceiling bookcases, floating shelves, narrow shelving units, built-in furniture, or other unused spaces. You can also mix books with [...]
body_text: The best book storage ideas make your collection easy to access while using your available wall, floor, and furniture space efficiently. Depending on the size of your collection and your home, you can store books on floor-to-ceiling bookcases, floating shelves, narrow shelving units, built-in furniture, or other unused spaces. You can also mix books with framed photos, plants, souvenirs, and other meaningful objects to create shelves that feel personal rather than purely functional. What Are the Best Ways to Store Books at Home? The best way to store books at home depends on the size of your collection and how much space you have. Bookcases and built-in shelves work well for larger collections, while floating shelves, book towers, corner units, and multifunctional furniture can help maximize smaller spaces. Whichever option you choose, keep books organized and avoid overcrowding shelves so individual books remain easy to access. How Can You Use Vertical Space for Book Storage? Floor-to-ceiling shelving can maximize wall space while giving a large book collection a dedicated place to live. It can work especially well in living rooms, home offices, bedrooms, or reading areas where floor space is limited. For a home-library feel, pair tall shelving with a reading lamp and comfortable chair. You can also build or arrange shelving around a window and add a window seat to combine book storage with a dedicated reading area. Floating shelves are another option when you want to use wall space without adding a full bookcase. They can be particularly useful for displaying smaller collections or favorite books. How Can You Store Books in a Small Space? In a small home or apartment, narrow bookcases, rotating book towers, corner shelves, and wall-mounted shelving can provide book storage without taking up as much floor space. Look for unused areas that could accommodate vertical storage, including corners, hallways, spaces beside furniture, and sections of open wall. Rotating book towers can provide access to books from multiple sides, while tall, narrow bookcases take advantage of vertical space rather than spreading a collection across the room. What Are Some Creative Book Storage Ideas? Furniture and underused areas of your home can provide additional book storage when traditional bookcases aren’t practical. Headboards with built-in shelves, for example, can provide bedroom book storage without requiring separate bedside tables. Deep open shelving can serve as both a bookcase and room divider, while leaving sightlines through the space. Other creative book storage ideas include: Under-the-stair shelving Built-in wall niches Window-seat shelving Trough-style shelves for desks or countertops Hidden-door bookcases Benches or other furniture with built-in shelving These options can help turn otherwise unused areas into functional storage. How Can You Organize Books by Color? Organizing books by spine color can turn a book collection into a visual feature. Arrange books in groups of similar colors or create a gradual transition from one color to another. You can also use color on the shelves themselves. Painting shelves and brackets the same color as the wall can create a more seamless appearance and allow the books to become the focal point. If you prefer a more functional system, organize books by author, genre, subject, or size instead. How Do You Style Bookshelves Without Making Them Look Cluttered? To keep bookshelves from looking cluttered, leave some open space and mix books with a limited number of decorative objects. Framed photos, plants, artwork, souvenirs, and other meaningful items can add variety without filling every available inch. Try a few simple arrangements: Stack three large books horizontally and place a small object on top. Group three to five decorative objects with different shapes and heights. Lean a framed photo or piece of art against the back of the shelf. Arrange several books vertically and finish the grouping with bookends or a plant. Once you’ve finished, step back and look at the shelf as a whole. Breaking up objects with similar heights, shapes, or materials can create more visual balance. How Do You Keep Bookshelves From Looking Crowded? Avoid filling every inch of a bookshelf if you want your collection to feel more organized. Leaving some open space between groupings can help individual books and decorative objects stand out. Lining up book spines at a consistent depth can also create a cleaner appearance. If you have books of different sizes, placing some of the tallest or heaviest books on lower shelves can help create visual balance. If you regularly add books to your collection, periodically reassess what you want to keep on display. How Should You Store Books You Don’t Have Room to Display? Books you don’t currently have room to display can be packed in sturdy boxes or containers and stored in a clean, dry location. Keep books away from moisture and avoid packing them so tightly that covers or bindings become damaged. Books you want to keep but don’t need regular access to can also be stored away from your primary living space. This can be useful for large collections, inherited books, textbooks, or books you rotate in and out of your home library. If books and other belongings are taking up too much space at home, a storage unit can provide additional room for items you want to keep but don’t need to display every day. Public Storage offers storage unit sizes for a variety of storage needs, including books, seasonal decor, furniture, and other household belongings. The right book storage setup doesn’t have to hide your collection. By using vertical space, choosing storage that fits your room, and giving your favorite books room to stand out, you can create a space that’s both functional and personal. FAQ What is the best way to store books at home? The best way to store books at home is to use shelving that fits your space and collection size, such as bookcases, floating shelves, or built-in storage. Keep books organized, supported upright, and avoid overcrowding shelves to prevent damage and make them easy to access. How do you store books in a small space? In small spaces, use vertical storage like tall narrow bookcases, wall-mounted shelves, corner units, or rotating book towers. Look for unused areas such as hallways, corners, and spaces above furniture to maximize storage without taking up floor space. Is it okay to store books flat or upright? Yes, both methods are acceptable. Most books are best stored upright with proper support to prevent leaning. Larger or heavier books can be stored flat to reduce strain on their spines and bindings. How do you keep books from getting damaged in storage? Store books in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight and moisture. Use sturdy boxes or containers if storing long-term, and avoid packing them too tightly. Make sure books are clean and fully dry before storing. Can books be stored in a storage unit? Yes, books can be stored in a storage unit as long as they are properly packed. Use durable boxes, keep them off the floor if possible, and avoid damp conditions. Climate-controlled storage is ideal for long-term preservation. How do you organize books on shelves? Books can be organized by genre, author, subject, size, or color. The best system depends on whether you prioritize function or aesthetics. Many people combine systems, such as grouping by genre and then arranging by color within each group. How do you make bookshelves look neat instead of cluttered? Leave some open space on each shelf and mix books with a few decorative items like plants, framed photos, or objects of varying height. Avoid overcrowding and group items in small, intentional clusters for a balanced look. What should you do with books you don’t have space for? Books you don’t have space for can be stored in labeled boxes in a dry, protected area or placed in a storage unit. This is especially useful for large collections, seasonal books, or items you want to keep but don’t need to access regularly.

title: The Best Perfume Subscription Boxes for 2026 (and How They Actually Work)
summary: Fragrance shopping used to mean spritzing a paper strip at the counter and hoping it translates well to your skin, or dropping $150 on a full bottle, only to find out, three wears in, that it wasn&…
body_text: Fragrance shopping used to mean spritzing a paper strip at the counter and hoping it translates well to your skin, or dropping $150 on a full bottle, only to find out, three wears in, that it wasn’t at all what you pictured in your head. Enter: the perfume subscription box, which exists to close that gap. If you want the short answer: a perfume subscription box suits anyone who wants to actually wear a wide range of fragrances without buying full bottles at a time. It’s a poor fit if you’ve already found your signature scent and have zero interest in trying anything new. But for everyone in between—those curious but not sure exactly what they like, or perhaps wanting to gift something more interesting than a gift car–a box is one of the lowest-risk ways to learn more about the plethora of fragrance notes that exist. How the Box Model Actually Works After stripping away the branding, practically every perfume subscription box runs on the same basic mechanic. You pick a plan, browse a catalog of fragrances, and each month, a small travel-size vial of your chosen scent shows up at your door. Most boxes let you swap your pick before it ships, or cancel outright without penalty. The vial itself is usually somewhere around 8 ml, enough for roughly a month of regular wear, which is exactly the whole point: you’re testing a real amount of a fragrance on your actual skin, deciding if it’s best for you. This size also happens to double as the ideal travel format , small enough to clear TSA’s carry-on liquid limit with plenty of room to spare. This very distinction matters more than people expect. Fragrance reads differently depending on skin chemistry, shifting over the course of a day as it dries down, so a quick spritz at a department store counter tells you almost nothing about how a scent will actually smell eight hours later, on you, and in your city’s climate . A full month with a travel vial tells you everything a paper strip can’t, namely: how it wears in different types of weather, whether it lingers into the evening, proving to be long-lasting, and whether it truly falls under your personalized fragrance wardrobe . What Makes a Good Perfume Subscription Box Not all subscription boxes are built the same, and the differences show up in certain places: Catalog size and range. Fifty fragrances is a novelty. Hundreds, spanning designer names and smaller niche perfumers, is an actual discovery tool, meaning you’ll actually find something new. Access model. Some services split the catalog behind paywalled tiers, so the cheapest plan only unlocks a fraction of what’s really available. Others give you the whole thing at one price, maybe with a small added cost on the newest or most premium releases. Flexibility. Can you pick more than one scent a month? Skip without a hassle? Gift it to someone else? Vial size and value. An 8 ml vial that lasts a month is a meaningfully different value proposition than a 2 ml sample that’s gone in a week. Price relative to what you’re getting. Not just the sticker price, but what it actually unlocks: catalog access, number of scents per month, and whether “premium” fragrances cost extra. How Scentbird’s Box Works Scentbird’s model is built around a catalog of over 1,000 designer and niche fragrances, with plans that let you choose one, two, or three scents a month depending on the subscription plan you choose. Every scent ships as an 8 ml travel vial, about 120 sprays, more than enough to properly live with a fragrance before deciding whether it earns a full-size bottle. A short fragrance quiz helps narrow things down if you’re starting from zero, matching recommendations to scent families you already gravitate toward rather than leaving you to scroll a few hundred options blind. Gift subscriptions run 3, 6, or 12 months, which solves the classic problem of buying a gift for someone whose taste you don’t actually know, better than most gift options can. It’s important to note than a handful of newer or higher-end releases sit behind a small additional fee on top of the base plan, so the very cheapest tier doesn’t unlock the entire catalog outright. It’s a minor caveat next to the flexibility of the multi-scent plans, but worth knowing going in. Two Different Ways Boxes Are Built Most perfume subscription boxes fall into one of two categories. The first category gives you broad, flat access to a large catalog at one price point, with the option to add more scents per month if you want. The second one gates its catalog behind multiple paid tiers, meaning the sticker price you see advertised often only unlocks a portion of what the service actually carries. Neither model is inherently wrong, but they lead to very different real-world experiences: one rewards curiosity by letting you explore broadly from day one, the other rewards commitment by charging more the deeper into the catalog you want to go. Vial size is also worth checking closely. A handful of boxes market themselves on price alone while shipping considerably smaller sample sizes, which sounds like a deal until you realize you’re running out of a scent you liked halfway through the month. How to Start Without Much Risk The lowest-risk way into any subscription box is to treat the first month as a single, low-stakes test rather than a commitment. Take a quick quiz or browse a few scent families via Scentbird’s Notes Library . Once something sounds appealing, make your decision, then actually wear it for a few weeks before deciding whether to keep going. If you’re on the fence about designer versus niche, gourmand versus fresh, or simply don’t have a strong opinion yet, don’t fret–that’s totally normal. It’s the entire reason this model exists instead of asking you to guess right the first time at full retail price. Scentbird’s plans start with exactly that kind of low-commitment first month, with the option to skip, swap, or cancel at any point after. If you’re still weighing whether a box makes more sense than buying full bottles outright, it’s worth thinking through how you actually wear fragrance day to day before deciding. The Bottom Line A good perfume subscription box isn’t simply about the discount. More than that, it’s about access to a catalog wider than any department store counter. The right one for you comes down to things like catalog range and how much flexibility you actually need. Another thing to consider is whether you’d rather explore broadly from the start or pay more to go deeper over time. Remember, finding fragrances meant for you doesn’t happen overnight; it’s an ongoing process of figuring out what actually feels like you, encouraging self-reflection.

title: CPS Announces Second Quarter 2026 Earnings

body_text: << Back Aug 4, 2026 CPS Announces Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Revenues of $121.4 million compared to $109.8 million in the prior year period Net income for the second quarter of 2026 increased 30% to $6.2 million Total portfolio balance eclipsed $4 billion, finishing the second quarter at $4.31 billion New contract purchases of $758 million in the second quarter, a 75% increase from the prior year second quarter LAS VEGAS, NV, Aug. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Consumer Portfolio Services, Inc. (Nasdaq: CPSS) (“CPS” or the “Company”) today announced earnings of $6.2 million, or $0.27 per diluted share for its second quarter ended June 30, 2026. This represents a 30% increase in net income compared to $4.8 million in the second quarter of 2025. Earnings per diluted share increased by 35% compared to $0.20 in the second quarter of 2025. Revenues for the second quarter of 2026 were $121.4 million, an increase of $11.6 million, or 10.6%, compared to $109.8 million for the second quarter of 2025. Total operating expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $112.4 million compared to $102.8 million for the 2025 period. Pretax income for the second quarter of 2026 was $9.0 million compared to pretax income of $7.0 million, an increase of $2.0 million or 30% from the second quarter of 2025. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, total revenues were $233.7 million, an increase of approximately $17.1 million, or 8% compared to $216.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Total operating expenses for the six months ended June 30, 2026, were $216.7 million, compared to $202.9 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. body_text: Protecting brain health may start decades before symptoms appear Dementia is often viewed as a condition associated mainly with older age, but researchers continue to find that decisions made during middle age can have a major influence on future brain health. A new long-term study suggests that maintaining healthy blood pressure, avoiding diabetes, and not smoking between the ages of 45 and 65 may help people enjoy significantly more years of life without dementia. The research found that people who avoided all three major risk factors experienced almost 13 more years without dementia compared with those who had all three risks. The findings add to growing evidence that protecting the heart and blood vessels can also protect the brain. Long-term research highlights the importance of midlife choices Researchers from New York University Langone Health followed more than 12,000 adults who did not have dementia at the beginning of the study. Participants were assessed at around age 55 and monitored for an average of 26 years. The study focused on three important health factors linked to dementia risk: High blood pressure Diabetes Smoking During the follow-up period, more than 3,000 participants developed dementia, while around 5,200 people died without developing the condition. Researchers compared dementia-free survival rates among people based on the number of risk factors they had. The results showed a clear difference between those who maintained healthier lifestyles and those who had multiple risk factors. Participants with none of the three risk factors lived an average of 30.1 years without dementia after the study began. Those with one risk factor had around 26.3 dementia-free years, while people with two risk factors had approximately 21 years. Those with all three risk factors experienced about 17 years without dementia. The difference between the healthiest group and those with all three risks was close to 13 years. Why blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking matter for the brain The brain depends on a healthy blood supply to function properly. Conditions that damage blood vessels can also affect brain health over time. High blood pressure can contribute to damage in the small blood vessels that supply the brain. This damage may increase the likelihood of problems affecting memory and thinking. Diabetes can also influence dementia risk because high blood sugar levels may contribute to inflammation, blood vessel damage, and changes in brain function. Smoking affects the body in many ways, including reducing oxygen supply, increasing inflammation, and damaging cardiovascular health. Since the brain relies heavily on a strong circulation system, smoking can have long-term consequences for cognitive health. The study’s findings support the idea that preventing or controlling these conditions earlier in life could help delay the onset of dementia. Experts say heart health and brain health are closely connected Experts have increasingly emphasized the connection between cardiovascular health and cognitive health. Dr Josef Coresh, director of the Optimal Ageing Institute at NYU Langone, said the research suggests people should actively work to avoid these risk factors during middle age to help preserve brain health for many years. Other researchers have highlighted that healthy habits such as regular physical activity, avoiding smoking, limiting excessive alcohol consumption, and staying socially connected may also support brain health. Dr Jacqui Hanley from Alzheimer’s Research UK noted that while there is no guaranteed way to prevent dementia, reducing risks linked to poor cardiovascular health may help lower the chances of cognitive decline. Professor Ian Maidment from Aston University said the findings add to previous research showing that what benefits the heart often benefits the brain as well. Women and dementia-free years The study also identified differences between groups. Researchers found that women generally lived longer without dementia than men, regardless of the number of risk factors they had. The research also reported differences in dementia-free years between racial groups, with white participants having more dementia-free years than black participants in the study population. Researchers noted that dementia risk is influenced by many factors, including genetics, environment, healthcare access, and social conditions. These findings highlight the importance of continuing research into how different populations experience dementia risk and prevention. Simple steps that may support brain health Although no lifestyle change can completely eliminate the possibility of dementia, experts recommend several actions that may support long-term brain health. Keep blood pressure under control Regular health checks can help identify high blood pressure early. Managing blood pressure through lifestyle changes and medical advice when needed may reduce risks linked to vascular damage. Prevent or manage diabetes Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels through balanced nutrition, physical activity, and appropriate medical care can support overall health and may help protect the brain. Avoid smoking Stopping smoking or never starting can provide benefits for circulation, heart health, and brain health at any age. Stay physically active Exercise supports cardiovascular health and may contribute to better cognitive function as people age. Maintain social connections Relationships, social activities, and mental engagement may also play a role in supporting healthy ageing. Dementia prevention begins before old age The latest research reinforces an important message: brain health is not only an issue for later life. The choices people make during their 40s, 50s, and 60s may influence how they age and how long they remain free from dementia. While researchers continue to study the complex causes of dementia, reducing known risk factors remains one of the most practical steps individuals can take. Maintaining healthy blood pressure, avoiding diabetes, and not smoking may provide benefits that extend far beyond physical health. Protecting the brain starts with protecting the body, and midlife may be a crucial opportunity to make changes that support healthier ageing. Source New York University Langone Health regarding midlife vascular risk factors and dementia-free survival. Disclaimer This article is for informational purposes only and is not medical advice. Individual dementia risk depends on many factors, including genetics, age, medical history, and lifestyle. Anyone concerned about dementia risk or health conditions should consult a qualified healthcare professional.

title: Maximizing ROI with Premium DOOH Inventory
summary: Securing high-value ad placements requires more than just budget; it demands Premium DOOH inventory.
body_text: Securing high-value ad placements requires more than just budget; it demands Premium DOOH inventory. This guide explores how advertisers can optimize campaigns by evaluating DOOH inventory quality, consolidating supply access, and utilizing intelligent advertising. Discover strategies to enhance performance measurement and targeting to maximize your return on investment. Key Takeaways Q: How do brands avoid wasting ad spend on low-visibility digital billboards? A: By securing Premium DOOH inventory through trusted platforms like Perion, which enforce strict standards for viewability, hardware, and data accuracy. Q: What is the main financial risk of using disconnected supply-side platforms? A: Fragmented buying causes duplicate bid inflation and hidden fees, making consolidated access to Premium DOOH inventory essential for protecting your budget. Q: How do dynamic data triggers improve outdoor campaign performance? A: By connecting live data like weather or traffic to Premium DOOH inventory, brands can serve highly contextual, engaging ads in real time. Q: How should marketers evaluate the true success of their outdoor campaigns? A: Instead of relying on impression estimates alone, brands should use proof-of-play reporting and footfall lift studies to evidence the ROI of their Premium DOOH inventory. Q: Why is demographic movement critical for programmatic outdoor buying? A: Mapping audience data to physical screens helps concentrate Premium DOOH inventory purchases on the times when the highest density of target buyers is nearby. Q: What is the best way to scale an outdoor advertising strategy across new markets? A: Advertisers must rigorously audit supply partners for transparency and utilize automated workflows to consistently secure Premium DOOH inventory. Defining the True Standards of DOOH Inventory Quality Not all digital billboards and transit screens deliver the same value to advertisers. Evaluating DOOH inventory quality requires a strict assessment of physical screen characteristics, location context, and the accuracy of the data tied to that specific placement. High standards prevent ad spend from being wasted on low-visibility or poorly maintained displays. Essential Metrics for Screen Evaluation Advertisers must look beyond basic location descriptions to understand the actual value of a screen. High-quality placements offer verifiable visibility, high-resolution displays, and accurate audience data mapping that aligns with specific campaign goals. Evaluation Metric Premium DOOH Inventory Standard/Low-Tier Inventory Viewability Unobstructed sightlines with long dwell times. Partially blocked by trees, buildings, or traffic signals. Ad Clutter Exclusive placements with limited screen rotation. High rotation loops where individual ads get lost. Hardware Quality High-definition, weather-resistant LED panels. Low-resolution screens prone to pixel burn or glare. Data Accuracy Independently measured location and audience data, such as Geopath or Route. Estimated or outdated demographic assumptions. Platforms like Perion prioritize these strict standards, helping advertisers concentrate bids on screens that meet stringent visibility and technical requirements. By filtering out low-tier placements, brands can allocate their budgets to screens that actively capture consumer attention and drive measurable results. Why Fragmented DOOH Inventory Drains Your Campaign Budget Purchasing digital out-of-home media across multiple disconnected supply-side platforms creates significant operational hurdles. Dealing with fragmented DOOH inventory often leads to overlapping bids, hidden technology fees, and inconsistent reporting that severely diminishes overall campaign return on investment. The Hidden Costs of Disconnected Supply When media buyers operate across too many independent exchanges, they lose the ability to control ad frequency and optimize their spending effectively. This fragmentation forces programmatic teams to spend hours reconciling data instead of optimizing creative delivery and strategy. Duplicate Bid Inflation: When multiple exchanges offer the exact same screen, advertisers can accidentally bid against themselves, artificially driving up the clearing price. Excessive Technology Fees: Each intermediary in a fragmented supply chain takes a percentage of the media spend, reducing the actual working budget that goes toward screen time. Inconsistent Reporting Standards: Different platforms measure impressions and play-outs differently, making it very difficult to determine the true reach of a cross-platform campaign. Loss of Frequency Control: Without a centralized buying path, it is incredibly difficult to cap how many times a specific consumer segment is exposed to an advertisement. Consolidating these buying paths is the most direct way to reduce these redundant costs. Advertisers who streamline their supply chains often see an improvement in their effective cost per thousand impressions (eCPM) and overall media efficiency. The Competitive Edge of Consolidated Inventory Access Transitioning away from a scattered buying approach allows advertisers to centralize their bidding strategies. Consolidated inventory access provides media buyers with a unified view of available screens, pricing dynamics, and audience movements across multiple media owners. Streamlining Supply Path Optimization Supply path optimization becomes highly effective when buyers route their budgets through a select group of trusted technology partners. This focused approach reduces latency in programmatic bidding and increases the share of working media spend that reaches publishers directly. Direct Publisher Integrations: Centralized platforms build direct pipelines to media owners, bypassing unnecessary intermediaries and reducing latency. Transparent Pricing Models: Buyers gain clear visibility into clearing prices and auction dynamics, allowing for more accurate bidding strategies. Unified Campaign Management: Media teams can manage pacing, budgeting, and creative delivery from a single interface, significantly reducing operational overhead. Enhanced Volume Discounts: Funneling more budget through fewer platforms often unlocks better pricing tiers and preferred access to high-demand screens. Working with partners like Perion allows brands to utilize centralized platforms that aggregate high-value screens into a single, manageable framework. This unified approach simplifies campaign execution while providing the scale necessary for national or global campaigns. Leveraging Intelligent Advertising for Maximum Brand Impact Static digital posters are no longer sufficient for capturing consumer attention in busy urban environments. Intelligent advertising utilizes real-time data inputs to adapt creative messaging based on the immediate context of the screen’s location. Dynamic Creative Optimization in DOOH By connecting external data feeds to programmatic DOOH campaigns, advertisers can trigger specific creative assets when environmental conditions change. This contextual relevance supports stronger ad recall and consumer engagement. Weather-Based Triggers: Retailers can automatically switch creative assets to promote umbrellas during rainstorms or cold beverages during heatwaves. Traffic and Transit Data: Automotive brands can display specific messaging when highway traffic slows down, capturing the attention of a captive audience. Time-of-Day Messaging: Quick-service restaurants can promote breakfast items in the morning and dynamically shift to dinner specials in the late afternoon. Live Sports Scores: Sports apparel brands, and betting apps in markets where gambling advertising is permitted, can display real-time game updates to engage fans near stadiums or sports bars. Implementing these dynamic triggers across Premium DOOH inventory helps the right message reach the consumer at the moment it is most relevant. This strategic alignment of creative and context can drive higher conversion rates for retail and direct-to-consumer brands. Modernizing Your DOOH Performance Measurement Evaluating campaign success based solely on estimated impressions is an outdated methodology. Modern DOOH performance measurement relies on proof-of-play logs, panel-based location data, and advanced attribution modeling to evidence actual business outcomes. Advanced Attribution and Outcome Tracking Advertisers require concrete proof that their digital out-of-home campaigns are driving foot traffic, web visits, or app downloads. By utilizing privacy-compliant, aggregated location data and measurement panels, brands can estimate the behavior of consumers after they are exposed to a screen. Measurement Category Legacy Methodologies Measurement Standards Audience Reach Static traffic counts and historical census data. Panel-based movement analytics and modelled audience impressions. Brand Lift General market surveys conducted post-campaign. Targeted mobile surveys delivered to panels matched to exposed audiences. Conversion Tracking Correlating sales spikes with campaign dates. Footfall lift against control groups, plus cross-device retargeting. Technology providers like Perion integrate these advanced measurement capabilities directly into the campaign reporting structure. This allows marketers to optimize their live campaigns based on actual conversion data rather than waiting for post-campaign wrap-up reports. Shifting Toward an Audience-Driven Targeting Strategy Traditional out-of-home buying focused primarily on the physical location of the billboard. Today, successful campaigns rely on an audience-driven targeting strategy that prioritizes the movement patterns and demographic profiles of the people passing by the screens. Mapping Mobile Data to Physical Locations By analyzing aggregated, anonymized mobile location data, advertisers can identify which screens over-index for their specific target demographics at different times of the day. This shifts the focus from buying locations to buying actual audiences. Historical Movement Analysis: Studying past behavior to predict where target demographics are most likely to travel during specific days of the week. Real-Time Audience Concentration: Adjusting bid modifiers to bid higher during the dayparts when the modelled concentration of the target demographic around a screen is highest. Cross-Channel Retargeting: Building addressable audience segments from consented, aggregated exposure data so that people likely to have passed a screen can be served sequential mobile ads, subject to regional privacy law. Custom Audience Segmentation: Building highly specific audience profiles based on shopping habits, app usage, or previous location visits. This data-centric approach helps concentrate budget on the times when the target audience is densest. It reduces wasted impressions and improves the overall efficiency of the programmatic DOOH buy. How to Audit and Select Your DOOH Supply Partners The quality of your digital out-of-home campaigns is directly tied to the reliability of your supply-side partners. Conducting a thorough audit of potential partners is crucial for maintaining brand safety and securing favorable pricing models. Criteria for Rigorous Partner Evaluation Media buyers must look beyond the sheer number of screens a partner offers and investigate the technical infrastructure supporting those screens. Transparency in auction dynamics and data collection methods is an absolute necessity for modern media buyers. 1. Verify Hardware Specifications: Request detailed documentation on screen resolution, maintenance schedules, and physical placement context to ensure high visibility. 2. Audit Data Privacy Compliance: Confirm that all location data used for targeting and measurement strictly complies with regional privacy regulations such as the GDPR and the CPRA, including a documented lawful basis for consent. 3. Evaluate Integration Capabilities: Test the supply-side platform for latency, bid request accuracy, and compatibility with your preferred demand-side platform. 4. Review Financial Transparency: Demand a clear breakdown of take rates, technology fees, and auction mechanics to prevent hidden costs. Partnering with established entities like Perion provides a layer of assurance regarding inventory quality and technical reliability. A strict auditing process materially reduces your exposure to ad fraud and technical delivery failures. Realizing Long-Term Scalability with Premium DOOH Inventory Achieving a high return on investment for a single campaign is a good start, but the ultimate goal is building a scalable media framework. Consistent access to high-quality screens allows brands to expand their geographic reach without sacrificing performance. Building a Sustainable Campaign Framework Scaling DOOH operations requires standardized buying protocols, automated creative delivery, and continuous performance feedback loops. Advertisers must establish workflows that can easily adapt to new markets and emerging screen formats. Automated Workflow Adoption: Reducing manual insertion orders in favor of programmatic guaranteed and private marketplace deals. Continuous A/B Testing: Running multiple creative variants across different environments to establish baseline performance metrics for future campaigns. Strategic Market Penetration: Using successful engagement metrics from primary markets to confidently expand buying strategies into secondary and tertiary cities. Cross-Format Standardization: Developing creative templates that easily adapt to various screen ratios, from vertical transit displays to horizontal highway billboards. By committing to a strategy centered on Premium DOOH inventory, brands can future-proof their outdoor advertising efforts. This commitment ensures sustained audience engagement, operational efficiency, and measurable revenue growth. Found this useful? Share it: Perion Marketing

title: The Cars We Wish We’d Bought 10 Years Ago
summary: They say hindsight is 20/20. In this case, hindsight is 2010, because there are a bunch of cars we wish we’d purchased back then. As we now realize the error of our ways, let’s not make the same mistake this year, shall we?
body_text: They say hindsight is 20/20. In this case, that hindsight takes us all the way back to the mid-2010s, a period which turned out to be a golden age of automotive bargains that most of us were simply too cash-strapped to capitalize on. Whether these vehicles have vanished from production entirely or quietly climbed to prices that are now out of reach, these are the cars we should have grabbed when we still had the chance. You didn't need a crystal ball to recognize their potential. You just needed money — which the Great Recession had a particularly cruel habit of making scarce. This list covers the full breadth of the automotive world: cars, trucks, and SUVs spanning virtually every segment, so there's something here to make every enthusiast groan with regret. As we come to terms with the missed opportunities of the past, let's make a commitment not to repeat those same mistakes in 2026 — and spare ourselves from writing this exact same article all over again in 2036. What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different The Cars We Wish We'd Bought 10 Years Ago 2009–2014 Acura TL SH-AWD 2008–2013 BMW M3 2011–2014 Cadillac CTS-V Wagon 2010–2013 Chevrolet Corvette Grand Sport 2006–2014 Honda Ridgeline 2009–2015 Jaguar XFR 2010–2013 Mazda Mazdaspeed3 2009–2014 Nissan Cube 2008–2009 Pontiac G8 GXP 2006–2012 Porsche Cayman S FAQs Shopping Tools Related Topics 2009–2014 Acura TL SH-AWD Around 2010–2011, Acura was going through a difficult stretch. The brand shed a staggering 19 percent of its market share in 2011 and recorded its worst sales year ever. And yet, it kept producing genuinely compelling vehicles engineered to go the distance. The Acura TL was one of those standouts. It was ultimately replaced by the TLX in 2015 — a solid car in its own right, and admittedly far more attractive than the TL's divisive "Power Plenum" grille. But the TLX arrived exclusively with an automatic: a nine-speed in the first generation, and a 10-speed in the current one. The TL, on the other hand, offered a six-speed manual — and you could pair it with what many consider the finest regular-production Acura ever built: the TL SH-AWD. At a time when manual transmissions were increasingly being relegated to base trims, finding one mated to an all-wheel-drive system was virtually unheard of. The SH-AWD also brought 305 horsepower to the party, a 19-horsepower improvement over the outgoing TL Type-S. Best estimates put total production of the manual SH-AWD at around 3,500 units, though Acura has never published a sales breakdown — meaning the actual figure could be even lower. Read our Overview of the Acura TL Search for Acura TL See all 2008 Acura TL $7,934 121,587 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Sandusky, OH 2012 Acura TL $13,315 96,263 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Greer, SC 2013 Acura TL $11,999 107,478 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal San Antonio, TX 2012 Acura TL $9,199 133,020 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Altamonte Springs, FL 2012 Acura TL $12,490 105,691 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal North Hills, PA 2013 Acura TL $13,098 111,499 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Lee's Summit, MO 2008–2013 BMW M3 Some things in life are simply guaranteed: the sun rises in the east, the IRS always finds you, and the BMW M3 will inevitably become too expensive for most people to afford. It's a pattern that has played out with every single generation of BMW's legendary performance sedan. There was a time when an E30 M3 could be had for $25K. That ship has sailed. There was a time when an E36 M3 sedan was priced below a Civic. Ancient history. These E90/E92/E93 M3 sedans, coupes, and convertibles are sitting right at the floor of the depreciation curve — and the opportunity to act may not stay open much longer. Once enthusiasts collectively recognize just how extraordinary these cars are, prices will move fast. And extraordinary they are: this was the only M3 ever powered by a V8, a magnificent unit producing 414 horsepower. It was also the first BMW to offer a dual-clutch gearbox as the automatic option, in the form of Getrag's outstanding seven-speed M-DCT. Even the heavier E93 Convertible could reach 60 mph in 5.1 seconds. Motor Trend once declared the E90/E92/E93 M3 "the greatest all-around car in the world." When that verdict was written, the M3 carried a $57,000 sticker. Today, you can find one for less than half that. Hunt down a low-mileage example with a thorough service history and you may find it outperforms your 401(k) over the next decade — while delivering one of the most rewarding driving experiences the modern era has produced. Read our BMW M3 Buying Guide Search for BMW M3 See all 2015 BMW M3 $35,390 72,223 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Honolulu, HI 2022 BMW M3 $60,065 54,435 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Newport Beach, CA 2018 BMW M3 $56,524 44,087 miles No additional dealer fees Good Deal Gurnee, IL 2018 BMW M3 $50,013 75,351 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Beaumont, TX 2023 BMW M3 $69,990 41,938 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Bellevue, WA 2017 BMW M3 $44,870 74,586 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Pompano Beach, FL 2011–2014 Cadillac CTS-V Wagon Every automotive journalist knows the archetype: the car that the press unanimously loves and the buying public unanimously ignores. In the 1990s, it was the Nissan Sentra SE-R — celebrated in every magazine, passed over at every dealership. The phenomenon is thoroughly documented and endlessly frustrating. From 2011 to 2014, Cadillac produced the CTS-V Wagon, and it might as well have arrived from the factory stamped "Auto Writer Spec." Everything about it was right: 556 horsepower, rear-wheel drive, a six-speed manual transmission, bold aggressive styling, a practical midsize wagon body, and — critically — it was available in brown (officially listed as "Mocha Steel Metallic"). The automotive press was unanimous in its praise. Buyers were unanimous in their indifference. Over its production run, only 514 of these wagons were built with the manual gearbox. Delete the sunroof and the numbers become even more striking: just 180 manual examples without one, plus 206 automatics. The rarest configuration of all — Stealth Blue, manual, no sunroof — exists in exactly two units. Today, a low-mileage example of that car could fetch around $70,000. The Grand Sport package also added wider fenders, staggered-width tires, Z06-sourced brakes with cross-drilled rotors and six-piston front calipers, lightweight forged aluminum wheels, a fully revised suspension, and a transmission cooler.
